subject: Nested bulk discount structure inquiry for hosted API

Subject: Pricing kickoff: question on multi-layer bulk discounts

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're starting to model hosting economics for an LLM-powered shopping assistant and have a couple of specific asks about your hosted API pricing:

- Do you support nested bulk discounts (e.g., a committed monthly token band + an additional volume discount that applies only to sustained throughput above a threshold)?
- How do you treat burst usage vs. sustained baseline for commitments? Any differences in rate application or true-up mechanics?
- Can you share a baseline per-1K-token price plus a worked example for 40B tokens/mo so we can compare to our internal forecasts?

I've attached a small sample of our expected monthly token distribution (fastretail_usage_sample.csv) to help.

Appreciate if you can loop in pricing and sales. We'd like a short one-pager we can take to procurement.

Best,
Claire

FastRetail

Subject: Re: Pricing kickoff: question on multi-layer bulk discounts

Hi Claire — thanks for the sample and the clear questions. Quick answers up front and we'll follow with a short matrix:

- Short answer: yes, we support nested structuring for hosted customers — a committed monthly token band (commit) + an incremental sustained-discount tier that applies once a sustained throughput threshold is observed for an agreed window.
- Bursts: bursts above sustained thresholds are billed as overage unless you configure burst add-on credits or a burst pool. Bursts that are short (seconds) can be absorbed by KV/prefix caching behavior and usually don't trigger higher rates if they fall within expected patterns.
- We'll produce a baseline per-1K-token rate and a worked example for 40B tokens/mo.

I've attached our baseline hosted ratecard (redwood_hosted_ratecard_v1.pdf) — it includes base rates, committed discounts, and our standard definitions for "sustained throughput" windows. Aditya — can you draft the 40B worked example + a simple nested discount matrix (commit bands, sustained add-on, burst pool) and share as a one-pager for Claire/ProcureOps? Ben — please call out any SLA credit language we should include for sustained throughput.

I'll tee up a 30-min call if Claire's team wants to review the matrix live.

Cheers,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing kickoff: question on multi-layer bulk discounts

Claire — thanks for the sample, I did a quick pass on a nested structure below. This is a working example (numbers illustrative) we can lock in once we agree on commit length and measurement windows.

1) Baseline hosted rate (model: open-llm baseline e.g., llama-variant): $0.90 per 1K tokens (pay-as-you-go)

2) 12-month committed bands (prepaid or contractual true-up):
- Commit band A: 0 - 5B tokens/mo => 20% discount off baseline => $0.72 / 1K
- Commit band B: 5B - 25B tokens/mo => 30% discount on incremental volume => $0.63 / 1K (incremental pricing on top of band A)
- Commit band C: 25B - 50B tokens/mo => 40% discount on incremental volume => $0.54 / 1K

3) Nested sustained-throughput add-on (applies only when sustained throughput >= 150 concurrent rps-equivalent for a continuous 10-minute window): additional 10% off the incremental rate for usage above the threshold (this rewards steady, predictable load).

4) Burst pool / short-duration credits: optional monthly burst credit bucket you can buy (helps avoid spikes being billed at overage). Unused credits do not roll automatically but can be escrowed on multi-year contracts.

5) Overage & true-up: monthly true-up at incremental band rates. If you miss commit in a billing period, you pay the difference at contract rates.

Worked example for 40B tokens/mo (12-mo commit):
- First 5B @ $0.72 => cost = $3,600
- Next 20B @ $0.63 => cost = $12,600
- Remaining 15B @ $0.54 => cost = $8,100
- Subtotal token cost = $24,300 (this is illustrative per-1K-token buckets — we'll convert to full $ with exact token counts in the spreadsheet)
- If sustained threshold met for the 15B above threshold, apply nested sustained add-on: 10% off incremental => subtract ~$810

Notes:
- We can offer a one-time signup credit or demo credits for a 30-day pilot to validate cost and latency.
- If you need rollovers or softer true-up mechanics, we can structure a custom clause in the SOW/contract (typical for enterprise procurement).

Irene — Ben flagged SLA credit language and payment term questions. Ben?

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Pricing Analyst | Redwood Inference

Claire — closing the loop: Aditya and I discussed measurement and SLA language with Ben. Quick bullets and next steps:

- Measurement: sustained threshold is measured as account-wide token/sec averaged over rolling 60s windows, with the sustained condition triggered when the 60s average exceeds the configured rps-equivalent for 10 consecutive minutes. We'll translate 150 rps-equivalent into tokens/sec based on your model profile once you confirm model mix (we used 8 tokens per request average for the worked example).
- Burst credits: by default unused burst credits do not roll, but for a 12+ month contract we can offer a 50% credit conversion into overage buffer if you miss by two consecutive quarters (to be included in SOW).
- Deliverables: Aditya will upload a one-page PDF with the full dollarized 40B example and +/-15% variance by tomorrow 11:00 AM PST. We'll include a plain-English line for procurement around true-up, rollover, and SLA credits.
